name: server.R
content:
# server.R

# the server is always a function with these three arguments in this order: input, output, session. 
# we don't call this function, Shiny calls it, once per user session, and passes in the right things. we just define it.
# input is where we read what the user selected. Access with dollar-sign notation: input$state.
# output is where we write things to send back to the UI. Assign with dollar-sign ($): output$selection_summary <- ...
# session is a bag of session-level information (which user, what browser, etc.). 


server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  # ============================================================
  # DEPENDENT DROPDOWNS — cascade based on user selections
  # ============================================================
  
  # PHN dropdown depends on state
  observeEvent(input$state, {
    freezeReactiveValue(input, "phn")
    phns_in_state <- master_data %>%
      filter(state == input$state) %>%
      pull(phn) %>%
      unique() %>%
      sort()
    updateSelectInput(session, "phn", 
                      choices = phns_in_state,
                      #heatmap table is empty when the app first loads. Switching PHN and coming back makes it appear.
                      #when the app starts, the dropdowns are populated in sequence
                      #state dropdown has a value (“VIC”). But, the PHN dropdown is still empty
                      selected = phns_in_state[1]) #forces the PHN dropdown to have a definitive first-choice value immediately when it’s populated.
    })
  
  # Drug dropdown on Tab 3 depends on outcome (using the mapping)
  observeEvent(input$outcome_single, {
    freezeReactiveValue(input, "drug_single") ## freeze the child before updating it
    drugs_for_outcome <- master_data %>%
      filter(outcome == input$outcome_single) %>%
      pull(drug) %>%
      unique() %>%
      sort()
    updateSelectInput(session, "drug_single", 
                      choices = drugs_for_outcome,
                      selected = drugs_for_outcome[1]) #same logic here (in case)
  })
  
  # Postcode dropdown on Tab 4 depends on selected PHN
  observeEvent(input$phn, {
    freezeReactiveValue(input, "pc")
    req(input$phn)
    pcs_in_phn <- master_data %>%
      filter(state == input$state, phn == input$phn) %>%
      pull(pc) %>%
      unique() %>%
      sort()
    updateSelectInput(session, "pc", 
                      choices = pcs_in_phn,
                      selected = pcs_in_phn[1]) # and here (in case)
  })
  
  # Reset button
  # observeEvent(input$reset, {
  #   updateSelectInput(session, "state", selected = "VIC")
  #   updateSelectInput(session, "outcome_single", selected = choices_outcome[1])
  # })
  
  # ============================================================
  # SELECTION SUMMARY — sidebar footer showing what's selected
  # ============================================================
  
  # output$selection_summary <- renderUI({...})
  # The thing called utput$selection_summary should be produced by running this render block
  # the name selection_summary is exactly the same as outputId = "selection_summary" in the UI
  # renderUI() is a function that takes a block of code (inside { }) 
  # and treats it as a syntax for producing a output (eg, summary info)
  # it re-runs automatically whenever any input it depends on changes
  # Shiny watches, and if input$xx changes, this render block runs again
  # The { } braces let us put multiple lines of code inside. 
  # The last expression in the block is what gets rendered as the output
  
  
  output$selection_summary <- renderUI({
    # req() -> ensure that values are available before proceeding with a calculation or action.
    req(input$state, input$phn) 
    n_pcs <- master_data %>%
      filter(state == input$state, phn == input$phn) %>%
      pull(pc) %>% n_distinct()
    
    div(
      # controls the vertical spacing between all the lines inside this block
      style = "line-height: 1.4;",
      # 'display: block' forces a new line automatically, allowing to set a margin
      strong("Currently viewing:", style = "display: block; margin-bottom: 1px;"),
      # br() -> pushes the next text to a new line
      
      br(), "State: ", input$state, 
      br(), "PHN: ", input$phn, #" • ", 
      br(), n_pcs, " postcodes",
      br(), "Data pooled 2017–2021"
    )
    
  })
  
  # ============================================================
  # Section 1: REGIONAL OVERVIEW
  # ============================================================
  
  output$heatmap_plot <- renderPlot({
    req(input$state, input$phn)
    plot_heatmap(master_data, 
                 target_state = input$state, 
                 target_phn   = input$phn)
  }
  #, res = 70
  )
  
  # commenting out all the `downloadHandler` functions throughout `server.R`
  
  # # downloading the heatmap plot
  # output$heatmap_plot_download <- downloadHandler(
  #   # returns the file name the user's browser will save as
  #   filename = function() {   
  #     paste0("Heatmap_", input$state, "_", input$phn,# "_", #Sys.Date(),
  #            ".png")
  #   },
  #   content = function(file) {
  #     p <- plot_heatmap(master_data,
  #                       target_state = input$state,
  #                       target_phn   = input$phn)
  #     ggsave(file, plot = p, width = 10, height = 15, dpi = 300)
  #   }
  # )
  # 
  # 
  
  output$heatmap_table <- renderDT({
    req(input$state, input$phn)
    get_heatmap_table(master_data,
                      target_state = input$state,
                      target_phn   = input$phn) %>%
      select(pc, #mean_age, seifa_score,
             drug, outcome,
             #obs_n_prev,
             obs_prev, #obs_n_ir,
             obs_rate,
             dist_diag_std, total_severity) %>%
      rename(
        "Postcode" = pc,
        # "Mean Age" = mean_age,
        # "SEIFA Score" = seifa_score,
        "Medication" = drug,
        "Outcome" = outcome,
        "Medication use (%)" = obs_prev,
        "Incidence rate (per 1,000 PY)" = obs_rate,
        "Severity score" = dist_diag_std,
        "Total Severity" = total_severity
      ) %>%
      datatable(
        rownames = FALSE, # hides the row numbers
        options = list(
          pageLength = 15,
          scrollX = TRUE,
          # customize the search box label
          language = list(
            search = "Search postcode:",
            searchPlaceholder = "e.g., 3795"
          ),
          columnDefs = list(
            # disables search for columns 2 through 11 (indices 1 through 10)
            # NOTE: If we uncomment columns above, we will need to change '1:6'
            list(targets = #1:10,
                   1:6, searchable = FALSE)
          )
        )
      )
  })


  
  # ============================================================
  # Section 2: MEDICATION × OUTCOME
  # ============================================================
  
  ## FIGURES
  
  ######### single_association
  output$single_association <- renderPlot({
    req(input$state, input$phn, input$outcome_single, input$drug_single)
    plot_association_ci(master_data,
                        target_drug    = input$drug_single,
                        target_outcome = input$outcome_single,
                        target_state   = input$state,
                        target_phn     = input$phn)
  })
  
  
  # # downloadHandler
  # output$single_association_download <- downloadHandler(
  #   filename = function() {   
  #     #drug, outcome, state, phn
  #     paste0("association_", input$drug_single,"_", input$outcome_single,"_", input$state,"_", input$phn, ".png")
  #   },
  #   content = function(file) {
  #     p <- plot_association_ci(master_data,
  #                              target_drug    = input$drug_single,
  #                              target_outcome = input$outcome_single,
  #                              target_state   = input$state,
  #                              target_phn     = input$phn)
  #     ggsave(file, plot = p, width = 9, height = 9, dpi = 300)
  #   }
  # )
  
  
  
  ######### single_gap
  output$single_gap <- renderPlot({
    req(input$state, input$phn, input$outcome_single, input$drug_single)
    plot_gap_ci(master_data,
                target_drug    = input$drug_single,
                target_outcome = input$outcome_single,
                target_state   = input$state,
                target_phn     = input$phn)
  })
  
  
  # # downloadHandler
  # output$single_gap_download <- downloadHandler(
  #   filename = function() {   
  #     paste0("gap_", input$drug_single,"_", input$outcome_single,"_", input$state,"_", input$phn, ".png")
  #   },
  #   content = function(file) {
  #     p <- plot_gap_ci(master_data,
  #                      target_drug    = input$drug_single,
  #                      target_outcome = input$outcome_single,
  #                      target_state   = input$state,
  #                      target_phn     = input$phn)
  #     ggsave(file, plot = p, width = 9, height = 9, dpi = 300)
  #   }
  # )
  # 
 
  ######### single_ranked
  output$single_ranked <- renderPlot({
    req(input$state, input$phn, input$outcome_single, input$drug_single)
    plot_ranked_ci(master_data,
                   target_drug    = input$drug_single,
                   target_outcome = input$outcome_single,
                   target_state   = input$state,
                   target_phn     = input$phn)
  })
  
  
  # # downloadHandler
  # output$single_ranked_download <- downloadHandler(
  #   filename = function() {   
  #     paste0("ranked_", input$drug_single,"_", input$outcome_single,"_", input$state,"_", input$phn, ".png")
  #   },
  #   content = function(file) {
  #     p <- plot_ranked_ci(master_data,
  #                         target_drug    = input$drug_single,
  #                         target_outcome = input$outcome_single,
  #                         target_state   = input$state,
  #                         target_phn     = input$phn)
  #     ggsave(file, plot = p, width = 9, height = 9, dpi = 300)
  #   }
  # )
  
  
  ######### single combination table
  
  output$single_table <- renderDT({
    req(input$state, input$phn, input$outcome_single, input$drug_single)
    
    get_summary_table(master_data,
                      target_drug    = input$drug_single,
                      target_outcome = input$outcome_single,
                      target_state   = input$state,
                      target_phn     = input$phn) %>%
      select(
        pc, 
        # mean_age, seifa_score, drug, outcome, 
        # obs_n_prev, 
        obs_prev, 
        # obs_n_ir, 
        obs_rate,
        dist_diag_std #,
        # total_severity
      ) %>%
      rename(
        "Postcode" = pc,
        # "Mean Age" = mean_age,
        # "SEIFA Score" = seifa_score,
        # "Medication" = drug,
        # "Outcome" = outcome,
        "Medication use (%)" = obs_prev,
        "Incidence rate (per 1,000 PY)" = obs_rate,
        "Severity score" = dist_diag_std#,
        # "Total Severity" = total_severity
      ) %>%
      datatable(
        rownames = FALSE,
        options = list(
          pageLength = 15, 
          scrollX = TRUE,
          language = list(
            search = "Search postcode:",
            searchPlaceholder = "e.g., 3777"
          ),
          columnDefs = list(
            list(targets = 1:3, searchable = FALSE)
          )
        )
      )
  })

  
  # ============================================================
  # Section 3: POSTCODE REPORT
  # ============================================================
  
  # single reactive that filters the data — all Tab 4 outputs consume this
  pc_data <- reactive({
    req(input$pc)
    filter_postcode(master_data, input$pc)
  })
  

  output$pc_header <- renderUI({
    h <- get_postcode_header(pc_data())
    
    req(h)
    
    # clean up the data for display
    display_pop <- format(round(as.numeric(h$dm_cohort)), big.mark = ",")
    display_remoteness <- gsub(" of Australia", "", h$remoteness) # removing " of Australia" and replaced it with nothing ("")
    display_combos <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", h$combos_shown) # extract ONLY the numbers from the "Combinations shown" eg, turns "16 combinations shown" into "16",
    
    layout_columns(
      # setting this to 4 automatically creates a 3x2 grid
      col_widths = 4,
      
      value_box(title = "Postcode",    value = h$postcode),
      value_box(title = "People with diabetes (approx.)",  value = display_pop),  #NDSS registrants (approx.)
      value_box(title = "Mean age",    value = h$mean_age),
      
      value_box(title = "SEIFA score", value = h$seifa_score),
      value_box(title = "Remoteness",  value = display_remoteness),
      value_box(title = "Combinations shown",    value = display_combos)
    )
  })
  
  
  output$pc_severity_plot <- renderPlot({
    plot_postcode_severity(pc_data())
  })
  
  
  # # downloadHandler
  # output$pc_severity_plot_download <- downloadHandler(
  #   filename = function() {
  #     paste0("postcode_", input$pc, "_severity", ".png")
  #   },
  #   content = function(file) {
  #     ggsave(file, plot = plot_postcode_severity(pc_data()), 
  #            width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300)
  #   }
  # )
  
  
  output$pc_summary_table <- renderDT({
    get_postcode_summary(pc_data(), all_combos = combo_grid) %>%
      select(outcome, drug, obs_prev, obs_rate, dist_diag_std) %>%
      rename(
        "Outcome" = outcome,
        "Medication" = drug,
        "Medication use (%)" = obs_prev,
        "Incidence rate (per 1,000 PY)" = obs_rate,
        "Severity score" = dist_diag_std
      ) %>%
      datatable(
        options = list(
          pageLength = 16, 
          scrollX = TRUE, 
          dom = "t",
          columnDefs = list(
            # first two columns aligned left
            list(targets = c(0, 1), className = "dt-left"),
            # last three columns aligned right
            list(targets = c(2, 3, 4), className = "dt-right")
          )
        ),
        rownames = FALSE
      )
  })
  
  
  # # downloadHandler
  # output$pc_summary_table_download <- downloadHandler(
  #   filename = function() {
  #     paste0("postcode_", input$pc, "_summary", ".csv")
  #   },
  #   content = function(file) {
  #     df <- get_postcode_summary(pc_data())
  #     readr::write_excel_csv(df, file)
  #   }
  # )



}

name: hcf_functions_v4.R
content:
# filter
filter_master <- function(data, target_drug, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE) { #default NULL = no PHN filter; checked below with is.null()
  
  # up to here, we can plot drug*outcome data by states
  out <- data %>%
    filter(drug == target_drug, outcome == target_outcome, state == target_state)
  
  # we need this line to be able to break down the state data to phn data, which is an extra option here (target_phn = NULL)
  if (!is.null(target_phn)) {
    out <- out %>% filter(phn == target_phn)
  }
  
  #and this for bayside health
  if (bayside_only) {
    out <- out %>% filter(bayside_region == "Bayside Health")
  }
  
  out # return the filtered data
}



# shared theme for all plots
theme_hcf <- function() {
  theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),        # the plot's inner layout (behind the data), white, no border
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),        # the outer plot area (around the axes), white, no border  
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),                                 # removes minor grid lines (major grid lines stay)
      
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),             # main plot title at the top
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14),                            # plot sub title
      plot.caption  = element_text(size = 14),                            # caption text at the bottom of the plot (muted grey)
      axis.title    = element_text(size = 14),                            # axis names ("Postcode", "Medication", etc.)
      axis.text     = element_text(size = 14),                            # tick labels along both axes
      legend.title  = element_text(size = 14),                            # the legend's heading (e.g. "Severity Score")
      legend.text   = element_text(size = 13),                            # legend labels/values
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0", color = NA),      # facet header strip,light grey background
      strip.text    = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)              # text inside facet headers (e.g. "HF", "MACE")
    )
}



plot_association_ci <- function(data, target_drug, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE) {
  
  plot_df <- filter_master(data, target_drug, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn, bayside_only)
  plot_year <- unique(plot_df$year)
  region_label <- if (bayside_only) "Bayside Health" else if (is.null(target_phn)) target_state else target_phn
  
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = obs_prev, y = obs_rate)) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = obs_prev_lci, xmax = obs_prev_uci),
                   height = 0, color = "darkorange", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = obs_rate_lci, ymax = obs_rate_uci),
                  width = 0, color = "darkorange", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(colour = "navy", alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", colour = "red", linewidth = 1.2, se = FALSE) +
    labs(
      title = paste0(target_drug, " usage vs. ", target_outcome, " IR\n(", region_label, "; ", plot_year, ")"),
      x     = paste0(target_drug, " use (%)"),
      y     = paste0(target_outcome, " IR (per 1,000 PY)")
    ) +
    # theme_minimal() +
    # theme(
    #   panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    #   plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    #   panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    # )
    theme_hcf()
}


plot_association_ci_panel <- function(data, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn = NULL,  bayside_only = FALSE, ncol = 2) {
  
  region_label <- if (bayside_only) "Bayside Health" else if (is.null(target_phn)) target_state else target_phn
  
  # look up which drugs belong to this outcome
  outcome_drugs <- data %>%
    filter(outcome == target_outcome) %>%
    pull(drug) %>% 
    unique()
  
  # build one panel plot per drug, starting from plot_association_ci() and overriding for compact display
  panel_plots <- map(outcome_drugs, ~ 
                       plot_association_ci(data, target_drug = .x, target_outcome = target_outcome, 
                                           target_state = target_state, target_phn = target_phn, bayside_only = bayside_only) +
                       labs(title = .x, x = "Use (%)", y = "IR (per 1,000 PY)") +
                       theme(
                         plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
                         axis.title = element_text(size = 8)
                       )
  )
  
  # stitch into a grid
  wrap_plots(panel_plots, ncol = ncol) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(target_outcome, " Medication–Outcome Association (", region_label, ")"),
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))
    )
}




plot_gap_ci <- function(data, target_drug, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE) {
  
  plot_df <- filter_master(data, target_drug, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn, bayside_only)
  plot_year <- unique(plot_df$year)
  region_label <- if (bayside_only) "Bayside Health" else if (is.null(target_phn)) target_state else target_phn
  n_hotspots <- sum(plot_df$hotspot)
  
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = diff_prev, y = ir_diff)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = prev_diff_lci, xend = prev_diff_uci, y = ir_diff, yend = ir_diff),
                 color = "navy", alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = diff_prev, xend = diff_prev, y = ir_diff_lci, yend = ir_diff_uci),
                 color = "navy", alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_point(color = "navy", alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
    labs(
      title    = paste0(target_drug, " vs ", target_outcome, "\n(", region_label, "; ", plot_year, ")"),
      y        = paste0(target_outcome, " gap (obs - expected IR)"),
      x        = paste0(target_drug, " gap (obs - expected use)")
    ) +
    # theme_minimal() +
    # theme(
    #   panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    #   plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    #   panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    # )
    theme_hcf()
}


plot_gap_ci_panel <- function(data, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE, ncol = 2) {
  
  region_label <- if (bayside_only) "Bayside Health" else if (is.null(target_phn)) target_state else target_phn
  
  # look up which drugs belong to this outcome
  outcome_drugs <- data %>%
    filter(outcome == target_outcome) %>%
    pull(drug) %>% 
    unique()
  
  # build one panel plot per drug, starting from plot_gap_ci() and overriding for compact display
  panel_plots <- map(outcome_drugs, ~ 
                       plot_gap_ci(data, target_drug = .x, target_outcome = target_outcome, 
                                   target_state = target_state, target_phn = target_phn, bayside_only = bayside_only) +
                       labs(title = .x, x = "Med Gap", y = "Outcome Gap") +
                       theme(
                         plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
                         axis.title = element_text(size = 8)
                       )
  )
  
  # stitch into a grid
  wrap_plots(panel_plots, ncol = ncol) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(target_outcome, " Care Gaps (", region_label, ")"),
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))
    )
}




plot_ranked_ci <- function(data, target_drug, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE, threshold = 1) {
  
  plot_df <- filter_master(data, target_drug, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn, bayside_only)
  plot_year <- unique(plot_df$year)
  region_label <- if (bayside_only) "Bayside Health" else if (is.null(target_phn)) target_state else target_phn
  
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = prev_diff_std, y = ir_diff_std)) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "darkgreen", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_segment(aes(xend = line_x, yend = line_y), color = "purple", alpha = 0.4) +
    ### CIs
    geom_errorbar(
      data = function(df) subset(df, dist_diag_std > 1),
      aes(ymin = ir_diff_lci_std, ymax = ir_diff_uci_std), 
      width = 0, color = "darkorange", alpha = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_errorbarh(
      data = function(df) subset(df, dist_diag_std > 1),
      aes(xmin = prev_diff_lci_std, xmax = prev_diff_uci_std), 
      height = 0, color = "darkorange", alpha = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = dist_diag_std), shape = 21, size = 2, color = "white") +
    
    geom_text_repel(
      aes(label = ifelse(dist_diag_std > threshold, as.character(pc), "")),
      size = 3,
      color = "black",
      box.padding = 0.4,
      point.padding = 0.3,
      max.overlaps = Inf
    ) +
    
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "navy",
      mid = "white",
      high = "red",
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = c(-4, 6),
      oob = squish,
      name = "Severity Score"
    ) +
    # guides() -> legend theme settings.
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
      barwidth = 10,
      barheight = 0.6,
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5
    )) +
    
    labs(
      title = paste0("Standardised ", target_outcome, " vs ", target_drug, " Gaps\n(", region_label, "; ", plot_year, ")"),
      subtitle = paste0("High-risk postcodes (severity score > ", threshold, ")"),
      x = paste0("Standardised ", target_drug, " gap (obs - expected)"),
      y = paste0("Standardised ", target_outcome, " gap (obs - expected)")
    ) +
    # theme_minimal() +
    theme_hcf() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom", 
      legend.direction = "horizontal",
    #   panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    #   plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    #   panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
    
}


plot_ranked_ci_panel <- function(data, target_outcome, target_state, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE, ncol = 2) {
  
  region_label <- if (bayside_only) "Bayside Health" else if (is.null(target_phn)) target_state else target_phn
  
  # look up which drugs belong to this outcome
  outcome_drugs <- data %>%
    filter(outcome == target_outcome) %>%
    pull(drug) %>% 
    unique()
  
  # build one panel plot per drug, starting from plot_ranked() and overriding for compact display
  panel_plots <- map(outcome_drugs, ~ 
                       plot_ranked_ci(data, target_drug = .x, target_outcome = target_outcome, 
                                      target_state = target_state, target_phn = target_phn, bayside_only = bayside_only) +
                       labs(title = .x, subtitle = NULL, x = "Std Med Gap", y = "Std Outcome Gap") +
                       theme(
                         legend.position = "none",  # hidden per-plot; shared legend added below via plot_layout(guides = "collect")
                         plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
                         axis.title = element_text(size = 8)
                       )
  )
  
  # stitch into a grid with one shared legend
  wrap_plots(panel_plots, ncol = ncol) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(target_outcome, " Care Gaps (", region_label, ")", "; severity score > 1"),
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))
    )
}


# heatmap
plot_heatmap <- function(data, target_state, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE) {
  
  region_data <- data %>%
    filter(state == target_state)
  
  if (!is.null(target_phn)) {
    region_data <- region_data %>% filter(phn == target_phn)
  }
  
  if (bayside_only) {
    region_data <- region_data %>% filter(bayside_region == "Bayside Health")
  }
  
  region_label <- if (bayside_only) "Bayside Health" else if (is.null(target_phn)) target_state else target_phn
  plot_year <- unique(region_data$year)
  
  pc_ranking <- region_data %>%
    group_by(pc) %>%
    summarise(total_severity = sum(dist_diag_std, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(total_severity))
  
  heatmap_data <- region_data %>%
    mutate(pc = factor(pc, levels = rev(pc_ranking$pc)))
  
  ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = drug, y = pc, fill = dist_diag_std)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    
    facet_grid(~ outcome, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "navy",
      mid = "white",
      high = "red",
      midpoint = 0,
      limits = c(-4, 6),
      oob = squish,
      name = "Severity score"
    ) +
    # guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    #   barwidth = 1.2,
    #   barheight = 5,
    #   title.position = "top",
    #   title.hjust = 0.5
    # )) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
      barwidth = 20,        # length of the horizontal bar (in text-line units)
      barheight = 0.6,      # thickness of the bar
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5     # centres the title above the bar
    )) +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Geographic Surveillance: Summary of Care Gaps\n(", region_label, "; ", plot_year, ")"),
      subtitle = "Postcodes ordered by total cumulative severity within this region. Red indicates high severity.",
      x = "Medication",
      y = "Postcode"
    ) +
    #JIM: Made a change above to the subtitle.
    # theme_minimal() +
    # theme(
    #   axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    #   axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6),
    #   panel.grid = element_blank(),
    #   strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0", color = NA),
    #   strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    # )
    theme_hcf() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),  #postcodes
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),                         #meds
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.direction = "horizontal"
    )
}


# tables
get_summary_table <- function(data, target_drug, target_outcome, target_state = NULL, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE, top_n = NULL) {
  
  filtered_table <- data %>%
    select(state, phn, pc, outcome, drug, mean_age, seifa_score, dist_diag_std, 
           obs_prev, obs_rate, obs_n_ir, obs_n_prev, bayside_region) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 2))) %>%
    arrange(desc(dist_diag_std)) %>%
    filter(drug == target_drug, outcome == target_outcome)
  
  if (!is.null(target_state)) {
    filtered_table <- filtered_table %>% filter(state == target_state)
  }
  
  if (!is.null(target_phn)) {
    filtered_table <- filtered_table %>% filter(phn == target_phn)
  }
  
  if (bayside_only) {
    filtered_table <- filtered_table %>% filter(bayside_region == "Bayside Health")
  }
  
  if (!is.null(top_n)) {
    filtered_table <- head(filtered_table, top_n)
  }
  
  return(filtered_table)
}


get_heatmap_table <- function(data, target_state, target_phn = NULL, bayside_only = FALSE, top_n = NULL) {
  
  region_data <- data %>%
    filter(state == target_state) 
  
  if (!is.null(target_phn)) {
    region_data <- region_data %>% filter(phn == target_phn)
  }
  
  if (bayside_only) {
    region_data <- region_data %>% filter(bayside_region == "Bayside Health")
  }
  
  pc_ranking <- region_data %>%
    group_by(pc) %>%
    summarise(total_severity = sum(dist_diag_std, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(total_severity))
  
  # keep only the top N postcodes (by total_severity), if requested
  if (!is.null(top_n)) {
    pc_ranking <- head(pc_ranking, top_n)
    region_data <- region_data %>% filter(pc %in% pc_ranking$pc)
  }
  
  region_data %>%
    left_join(pc_ranking, by = "pc") %>%
    select(state, phn, pc, mean_age, seifa_score, drug, outcome, 
           dist_diag_std, obs_prev, obs_rate, obs_n_prev, obs_n_ir, total_severity) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 2))) %>%
    arrange(desc(total_severity), pc, desc(dist_diag_std))
}

# Header stats
get_postcode_header <- function(data_pc) {
  
  first_row <- data_pc %>% slice(1)
  n_shown   <- nrow(data_pc)
  
  list(
    postcode      = first_row$pc,
    phn           = first_row$phn,
    state         = first_row$state,
    year          = first_row$year,
    #population    = first_row$pop,
    dm_cohort    = (first_row$obs_N_prev)/5,
    mean_age      = round(first_row$mean_age, 1),

    remoteness    = first_row$aria,
    combos_shown  = paste0(n_shown, " combinations shown")
  )
}





get_postcode_summary <- function(data_pc, all_combos = NULL) {
  
  fmt_ci <- function(est, lci, uci, digits = 1) {
    ifelse(
      is.na(est),
      "Insufficient data",
      paste0(formatC(est, digits = digits, format = "f"),
             " (", formatC(lci, digits = digits, format = "f"),
             "–", formatC(uci, digits = digits, format = "f"), ")")
    )
  }
  
  # if no combo grid passed, use what's in data_pc (won't include missing combos)
  if (is.null(all_combos)) all_combos <- data_pc %>% distinct(outcome, drug)
  
  data_pc %>%
    right_join(all_combos, by = c("outcome", "drug")) %>%
    mutate(
      obs_prev      = fmt_ci(obs_prev, obs_prev_lci, obs_prev_uci, digits = 1),
      obs_rate      = fmt_ci(obs_rate, obs_rate_lci, obs_rate_uci, digits = 1),
      exp_rate      = ifelse(is.na(exp_rate), "–", 
                             formatC(exp_rate, digits = 1, format = "f")),
      dist_diag_std = round(dist_diag_std, 2),
      obs_n_prev    = ifelse(is.na(obs_n_prev), NA_integer_, as.integer(obs_n_prev)),
      obs_n_ir      = ifelse(is.na(obs_n_ir),   NA_integer_, as.integer(obs_n_ir))
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(dist_diag_std)) %>%
    select(outcome, drug,
           obs_prev, obs_rate, exp_rate,
           dist_diag_std, obs_n_prev, obs_n_ir)
}





# Severity plot
plot_postcode_severity <- function(data_pc) {
  
  plot_df <- data_pc %>%
    mutate(direction = ifelse(dist_diag_std > 0,
                              "Worse than expected",
                              "Better than expected"))
  
  pc_label     <- unique(data_pc$pc)
  region_label <- unique(data_pc$phn)
  plot_year    <- unique(data_pc$year)
  
  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = dist_diag_std, y = drug, colour = direction)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "gray50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = dist_diag_std, yend = drug), linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("Worse than expected" = "firebrick",
                 "Better than expected" = "navy"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    labs(
      title    = paste0("Postcode ", pc_label,
                        ": care gap severity across all combinations"),
      subtitle = paste0(region_label, "; ", plot_year),
      x        = "Standardised severity score",
      y        = NULL,
      caption  = "Only combinations with data are shown. Missing combinations shown in the table as 'Insufficient data'"
    ) +
    # theme_minimal() +

    #   panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),

    #   panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    #   strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0f0f0", color = NA),
